sanjay: Quick question — thinking about a proxy that handles both gRPC and JSON routes and applies unified quota/backpressure. Anyone tried a 'protocol-aware router' instead of transcoding? Thoughts on ergonomics + rollout UX?

julia: We prototyped a protocol-aware router last quarter. Pros: lower CPU on edge (no transcoding), can route directly to backend types. Cons: client surface gets messy (some teams still want single HTTP SDK) and telemetry can split. Will paste the config we used.

julia: ```yaml
routes:
  - match: /v1/embedding/*
    protocol: grpc
    route_to: embedding-pool-grpc
    quota_policy: customer_token_key
    backpressure:
      strategy: queue_length
      threshold: 500
      max_wait_ms: 120
  - match: /v1/chat/*
    protocol: http_json
    route_to: chat-frontend
    quota_policy: customer_token_key
    backpressure:
      strategy: concurrency
      limit: 50
```

mike: I'd prefer gateway-side transcoding for the public-facing endpoints so frontend teams get a single HTTP SDK. Easier for product devs. But yes — adds ~20-30ms p99 in our small tests. Quotas are simpler when everything is JSON.

tara: Transcoding added ~25ms p99 in our internal run (with 8k token requests). But it gave better logs/metrics for FE teams. We propagated request_id and customer headers which made spike debugging easier.

oliver: How do we attach quotas consistently? Streaming gRPC calls don't map 1:1 to JSON unary calls. Do we quota per-request, per-token, or per-stream?

julia: We implemented a 'quota key' abstraction: extractors can pull from headers or proto fields. Fallback: x-customer-id || proto.user.id || token.sub. That let us apply the same billing key across protocols.

sanjay: If we go protocol-aware, console needs to show per-protocol latency and per-model quota burn. Can the console support attribution split (grpc vs json) in the rollups?

mike: Console can do it, but route config must emit route_labels in traces (e.g., route.protocol, route.variant). Also the rate-limiter must attach metadata (quota_key, route_label) to metrics. Without that, attribution is fuzzy.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started for proto-router v0.3 -> edge-nodes (5% traffic).

tara: During the canary we saw adaptive backpressure thrash: queues filled then dropped, causing flapping on small hosts. Suggest smoothing window and queue-length-based shedding instead of instant cut.

oliver: Example pseudo-config we used to stabilize: ```json
{
  "backpressure": {
    "strategy": "queue_length",
    "threshold": 300,
    "smoothing_ms": 1000,
    "decay_ms": 5000,
    "shedding_pct": 0.1
  }
}
```

julia: Also consider fallback model variants on overload: auto-fallback to a cheaper/quantized model when latency or queue > threshold. MUST surface fallback events in console and have automatic rollback if quality regressions spike.

sanjay: Action items: 1) Perf matrix comparing transcode vs protocol-aware (p50/p95/p99 + CPU). 2) Quota key extractor proposal + proto field mappings. 3) Console story: per-protocol attribution + fallback signals. Who owns (1)?

mike: I'll run perf tests this week and post numbers. @julia can you share the proto->json mapping we used?

julia: Sharing minimal mapping snippet: ```python
# proto->json mapping (edge shim)
mapping = {
  "ChatRequest.user_id": "headers.x-customer-id",
  "EmbeddingRequest.customer_token": "headers.authorization",
  "StreamRequest.stream_id": "headers.x-stream-id || proto.stream.id"
}
```

tara: Noted. I'll add smoothing to the canary backpressure config and re-run tonight, will report stability metrics.

mike: thx :thumbsup!
